newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker with U.S. after data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker with U.S. after data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Tuesday, taking most of their direction from softer U.S. Treasuries, which weakened amid a mixed bag of economic reports, analysts said.

"It's mostly U.S. driven today. Yesterday was Canadian currency driven, but that's not the factor today. It's the U.S. market," said Hank Cunningham, director of fixed income for First Marathon Securities.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.43 to C$116.10 to yield 6.741 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 10/32 to yield 6.72 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to two basis points, from three basis points at Monday's close.

Both Canadian and U.S. bond markets began the session weaker, even though consumer price index reports for May showed inflation is subdued in both countries. Statistics Canada this morning reported core CPI in Canada in May rose 1.7 percent year-over-year, below expectations of a 1.8 percent rise.
However, U.S. industrial production and capacity utilization reports released later in the morning were stronger than expected.
Sharp gains in Canadian and U.S. markets in the past several sessions were also partly responsible for today's weakness, analysts said.
"The technicians are having a field day here. The market was extremely overbought. There's no question about that," said Cunningham.
Dealers said the Canadian market was also feeling the effect of recent new issues, including bonds from the provinces of Ontario and Quebec.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.30 to C$107.92 to yield 6.172 percent, while the U.S. 10-year fell 6/32 to 6.43 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 26 basis points from 27 basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.81 percent against its U.S. equivalent. which yielded 5.05 percent.
